key_insight: Nb and Ta preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B₂, consistent with lower boundary energies and favorable changes in metal–boron bonding.
engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary chemistry could strengthen high-entropy diboride ceramics without changing their overall composition.
method: DFT calculations of four grain-boundary types in five binary diborides and HEB₂.
COHP analysis of metal–boron bonding near the Fermi level.
Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics sampling of six HEB₂ boundaries using a fine-tuned MACE potential.
evidence_signal: Nb and Ta enrichment occurred at five of six sampled boundaries at 2000 K; at 300 K, a segregated Σ193 boundary sustained 26 GPa in tension versus 20 GPa for a chemically random boundary.
watch_item: The reported strengthening is computational and demonstrated for one boundary type; experimental validation and broader boundary sampling are needed.
paper_title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties
